engagements.name: Northwind Retail — Flagship Store
engagements.subtitle: Full authorised wireless penetration test (professional assessment)
engagements.summary: A complete engagement package: brief, scope, rules of engagement, target information, an AP inventory, an artefact bundle and a marking guide. No vulnerabilities are disclosed. You plan the test, choose the evidence, derive severity from impact, and write a client-ready report plus a retest plan.
client_background: Northwind Retail operates 12 stores and one small data centre; wireless is managed centrally by a two-person infrastructure team.
The Flagship Store has a retail floor, a back office with POS terminals (wired), a stock room, and a customer seating area with an outdoor overflow.
Wireless is used by staff laptops, handheld stock scanners, printers, customer devices and the guest portal.
The store previously had an incident where an unknown device was found plugged into a switch port; management is sensitive to rogue infrastructure.
objectives: Assess the security of the wireless infrastructure at the Flagship Store.
Determine whether an unauthorised party within RF range can obtain network access.
Assess separation between guest, retail/operations and corporate/enterprise traffic.
Produce a report that a remediation supplier can act on, including evidence and retest criteria.

in_scope: The four SSIDs listed under Target Information, at the Flagship Store only.
RF testing within the store footprint (and the seating area's outdoor overflow) during the agreed window.
One read-only RADIUS server configuration review.
The two provided test accounts on the enterprise SSID.
Passive capture, offline audits, rogue-authenticator testing on the guest SSID, and targeted deauthentication of the two provided test clients.
out_of_scope: All other stores and the corporate data centre network.
Physical attacks on POS hardware, the payment gateway, or staff devices.
Denial-of-service testing against production during trading hours (08:00–19:00).
Any interference with neighbouring organisations' networks.
Testing the guest portal's backend application (web application testing is a separate engagement).
prohibited: Capturing customer payload data beyond what the guest SSID exposes passively to any observer; no session-token replay against real customers.
Using real customer credentials in any test.
Changing any production configuration (including the RADIUS server and the AP settings).
Attacking, redirecting or deauthenticating any device other than the two provided test clients.
scope.windows: Passive testing 08:00–19:00 any business day. Intrusive tests (rogue authenticator, targeted deauth) only on Tuesdays/Thursdays 19:00–21:00, and only with the store manager's confirmation on the day.

roe_clauses: Authorisation: signed by the Northwind Retail CIO (named in the annex), valid for the agreed test window; the store manager is the on-site contact.
Technique matrix: passive capture (any time), offline audits (any time), rogue authenticator on NW-Guest (window only), targeted deauth on the two test clients (window only).
Safety: maximum transmit power per the local regulatory domain (`iw reg get`); no interference with neighbouring premises; each intrusive test has a documented rollback.
Data handling: captures encrypted at rest, retained 30 days after report acceptance, then deleted; no personal data in the report.
Evidence standard: captures delivered with SHA-256 hashes, filters and frame numbers; raw captures remain with the client.
Stop conditions: any disruption to POS or staff devices, any suspected real-world attack in progress, or any test that cannot be bounded — stop, notify, document.
Disclosure: critical findings notified within 4 hours; report due 10 business days after testing completes.

provided_artefacts.item: Site topology diagram and AP placement plan
provided_artefacts.note: Store, stock room, back office, seating area; 4 APs planned

provided_artefacts.item: AP inventory (BSSID, site, channel plan, firmware baseline)
provided_artefacts.note: With two 'unknown' entries flagged by the client
Artefact bundle A — beacon, recon, traffic, handshake, PMKID, WPS, WPA3, deauth, rogue, portal, EAP, RADIUS (the 16 lab captures)

provided_artefacts.item: RADIUS authentication and accounting logs for one business day
provided_artefacts.note: Includes a burst of failures for one service account

provided_artefacts.item: Guest portal redirect rules and session handling notes
Two test accounts (nw-test-01, nw-test-02), enterprise SSID only
provided_artefacts.note: Credentials in the annex; never use other accounts

deliverables: Reconnaissance and attack-surface inventory (frame-referenced, with stated limits).
Test plan derived from the brief and RoE, with each intrusive test mapped to its authorising clause.
Findings: claim, evidence, method, interpretation, impact, severity justification, remediation, retest criteria.
Evidence appendix: capture hashes, filters, frame numbers, config excerpts, log lines, reproduction steps.
Retest results against the remediated artefacts supplied at the end of the assessment.
Executive summary for the store manager (no jargon, no unverifiable claims).

tasks.title: Attack-surface inventory
tasks.detail: Enumerate every BSS and client visible in the artefact bundle; classify policy (AKM, ciphers, PMF, WPS, OWE) with frame numbers. State the limits of the capture.

tasks.title: Test plan
tasks.detail: Turn the brief and RoE into a sequencing plan: what you test, in what order, with what authorisation, and what you deliberately will not test.

tasks.title: Non-intrusive assessment
tasks.detail: From the artefacts and configuration excerpts, determine which weaknesses exist without transmitting anything. Justify each candidate finding with the exact artefact.

tasks.title: Key material analysis
tasks.detail: Audit the PSK-based SSIDs offline using the documented lab wordlist; relate each result to the environment (what the key actually grants).

tasks.title: Enterprise path analysis
tasks.detail: Reconstruct the 802.1X/EAP/RADIUS flow; determine what is exposed and under which precondition; verify one RADIUS integrity attribute where the material allows.

tasks.title: Segmentation and isolation
tasks.detail: Design and (using the captures/logs) evaluate the tests that prove or disprove guest isolation and inter-VLAN restriction. State what the artefacts do not prove and what you would run on site.

tasks.title: Findings and impact
tasks.detail: Write each finding with severity derived from this environment, quoting CVSS only as an example vector with justification.

tasks.title: Report and retest plan
tasks.detail: Assemble the report with an executive summary, prioritisation and per-finding retest criteria; execute the retest against the remediated artefacts and record pass/fail.

marking_guide.looks_like: Only in-scope targets tested; prohibited techniques avoided and the decision documented.
Complete inventory with frame numbers, ESS/look-alike analysis, explicit limits.
Correct frame/IE/protocol reasoning, correct tools and hashcat modes, no deprecated field names.
Every claim traceable to a hash + filter + frame number; screenshots never load-bearing.
Severity derived from the environment; technique labels never used as severity.
Specific, owned controls and a retest a third party can execute.
Clear structure, prioritisation, and an executive summary with no unverifiable claims.

notes: There is at least one red herring: a configuration that looks severe but is not reachable or not exploitable in this environment. Say so, and say why.
At least one SSID yields no exploitable weakness. Document the test you performed and the control that held — that section is graded.
If a test is not authorised or not safe, record why you did not perform it and what you did instead.
Timebox: no more than 40% of your effort on any single SSID.
